- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., Example 1, 2, 3).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or is low (e.g., Example 4, 5).
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecasts when sentiment volatility is high.
- Forecast horizon 30d often shows mean reversion bias — model holds too high or too low for extended periods; adjust toward recent 10-15d average if sentiment is weak.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3-5 days, model tends to overshoot; reduce forecast peak by 5-10% if sentiment > 0.6.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often undercorrects — add 2-5% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trend if sentiment diverges from price direction (e.g., sentiment rising but price falling — Example 4).
